full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury J: The plaintiff, now respondent No. 1 instituted in the Court of Assistant Judge, Madaripur, a suit being Title Suit No. 131 of 1985 for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in respect of 0.05 acre of non-agricultural land within Madaripur Pourasava. It is his case that Jagabandhu Baruri took settlement of the disputed land from Madaripur Pourasava by means of a registered kabuliyat of the year 1943. Jagabandhu Baruri died leaving three sons, Dwarikanath, Barada Kanta and Sarada Kanta as his heirs who continued possessing the said land on payment of rent. The disputed land was, however, wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No. 4, As a cloud was cast over the title of the Baruri brothers they brought Title Suit No. 268 of 1997 claiming title thereto and obtained an ex parte decree on 16 February 1978. On 21 November 1980 the said Baruri bothers transferred their interest in the disputed land in favour of Narayan Chandra Shaha who was also inducted into possession thereof. Subsequently Narayan Chandra Shaha sold the said land to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 11 August 1985. But defendant Nos. 2 and 3 having no title thereto trespassed into the disputed land thereafter. 

 9. The learned Counsel for the petitioner next attempts to argue that the kabuliyat of jagabandhu Baruri having not been followed by a patta executed by Madaripur Pourasava the settlement of the disputed land in favour of Jagabandhu Baruri is violative of section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act. This question was not agitated before the High Court Division. Moreover, we see no substance in it on the facts and in the circumstances established in the case.
